column1: # The golden corpus of file names: what MediaName must read from each one. One row per name, tab separated:
#   raw name <TAB> title <TAB> year <TAB> season <TAB> episode <TAB> part <TAB> extra
# An empty column means "none" (no year, not an episode, not a part, not an extra); it is checked, not skipped.
# extra is an ExtraKind: Trailer, Teaser, Promo, Sample or Extra. In a raw name, \uXXXX is the character with that code.
# A line starting with # is a comment, a blank line is ignored.
# A row goes in only when the right answer is certain from what the name says (the survey in private/name-survey,
# or a report a person sent). The expected value is written from the name, never copied from what the parser says.
# A name with two defensible readings goes in ambiguous.tsv; one whose answer is certain but the parser misses
# goes in known-gaps.tsv. NameGoldenCorpusTest runs this file and fails with a diff of every row that differs.
# A channel's handle in front, in every shape real chats post it (HX31; names from MSB and Cinema Paradiso, 2026-10-31)
# The same handle with a space, as it reads in a grid
# DVDWO in front of the title is a release tag, not a word of it
# A zero width space and a variation selector in front of a title
# A percent-encoded character is the character
# A year run into its resolution
# A channel's language word after the title
# A tilde in front, and titles that are only a name
# A title in its own script survives beside a Latin one
# The spellings one title goes by are each read as written (N3 folds them, the parser does not)
